organizations/irvine-taiwanese-presbyter.title: Irvine Taiwanese Presbyterian Church (IRVINE台灣基督長老教會)
organizations/irvine-taiwanese-presbyter.content:
Irvine Taiwanese Presbyterian Church (IRVINE台灣基督長老教會)
Summary
蒙上帝的恩典和祝福，我們是一群從台灣出生，蒙神帶領來到美國，經歷跨文化的衝擊，認真接受專業教育訓練與努力工作並培育子女，又蒙神眷顧及恩典滿滿的基督徒。我們大都從全美國退休，移居離台灣最近及安全舒適誼居的Irvine及Laguna Woods Village。我們愛台灣、愛美國、我們相愛相扶持，並努力遵行上帝的旨意，繼續尋求上帝的旨意，希望我們還能多為主做工。 邀請您來到我們這愛的大家庭，一起把上帝的愛帶到Irvine我們教會與世界的每個角落。 自從我們得到了這間兄弟教會Geneva Presbyterian Church的愛心和包容，我們於2012年開始搬到Laguna village CA後，就在這個教會的Chapel做禮拜敬拜上帝，宣講主的福音，相愛相扶持過著黃金的歲月。
Official site

www.irvinetpc.org/

people/albert-s-lai.title: Dr. Albert S. Lai (賴信雄)
people/albert-s-lai.content:
Dr. Albert S. Lai (賴信雄)
Dr. Albert S. Lai (賴信雄, Lai Sin-hiong) is a Taiwanese American pastor, theologian, and foundational interpreter of Taiwanese immigrant church formation in North America.
Identity Snapshot

Era: 1960s–2020s legacy arc (1971 dissertation; 2025 republication context)
Geography: Taiwan → Southern California
Core roles: pastor, theologian, institution-builder, public witness voice

Testaments / Voice
Testament 1

“For various reasons, mainly political … a modern style of exodus.”


Date/Period: 1971
Context: Chapter III framing in Toward A Community of Hope — A Mission to Formosan Community in Los Angeles
Source: Primary Source Extracts
Source tier: A-tier (primary dissertation text)

Testament 2

“A man living in a period of transition searches for knowledge of the future…”


Date/Period: 1971
Context: Chapter VI constructive-theology framing
Source: Primary Source Extracts
Source tier: A-tier (primary dissertation text)

Testament 3

“Since everyone agrees that this dissertation still holds publishing value over 50 years later, I am, of course, willing and eager to facilitate its publication.”


Date/Period: 2025 republication context
Context: Author reflection in republication materials
Source: Republication Voices and Testaments (2025)
Source tier: A (direct first-person quotation in republication material)

Historical Context
Dr. Lai’s life-work sits at the junction of migration-era pastoral care and institution formation. In 1970 he participated in founding-era momentum around Formosan Presbyterian Church in Los Angeles (FPCLA), and in 1971 produced a dissertation that connected historical memory, migration pressure, identity tension, and communal mission.
Contributions and Legacy

Documented an early Taiwanese American migration/church framework in Toward A Community of Hope — A Mission to Formosan Community in Los Angeles. — Source: Toward A Community of Hope — A Mission to Formosan Community in Los Angeles (A)
Helped articulate church as both ethnic refuge and public mission community in Los Angeles founding-era context. — Source: Chapter IV analysis (A/B)
Became a cross-generational reference point through 2025 republication efforts linked to NTPC. — Source: book page republication notes (C)

Source Notes and Confidence
Source Confidence Legend


A-tier: direct quotations or primary-source textual attributions from the currently attached source set.


B-tier: near-contemporary attributed references or secondary materials closely tied to the event/person.


C-tier: compiled contextual interpretation layers that require further primary-source confirmation.


High confidence: dissertation authorship, year, and core themes (A)


Medium confidence: detailed pastoral episodes summarized from current compiled pages (B/C)


Needs verification: precise dates/locations of all founding worship events and internships


Name Variants / Disambiguation

English: Albert S. Lai
Chinese: 賴信雄
Romanization variant in some contexts: Lai Sin-hiong

Contribution Invitation
Use the shared intake process at Echopedia Community Contributions Hub and include:

Person/page name
Your relationship to the person/event
Memory/quote/correction text
Date or estimated period
Source type and permission status

Your contribution helps preserve this life record with both dignity and historical traceability.

people/leonard-hsu-jr.title: Leonard Hsu Jr. (許景鴻)
people/leonard-hsu-jr.content:
Leonard Hsu Jr. (許景鴻 / Hsu Ching-Hung)
Summary
Leonard Hsu Jr. (許景鴻 / Hsu Ching-Hung) is a Taiwanese American community organizer, systems builder, and the current President of the Taiwanese American Historical Society (台美人歷史協會). He leads Echo System and Echopedia initiatives focused on preserving Taiwanese American history, identity documentation, and community memory infrastructure.
Identity

Chinese name: 許景鴻 (Hsu Ching-Hung)
Correction note: 陳乃光 belongs to Rex Chen and should not be listed as Leonard Hsu Jr.’s Chinese name.

TAHS Leadership

President (會長), Taiwanese American Historical Society (台美人歷史協會)
Tax ID: 46-4005384 (501(c)(3) public charity, reinstated June 2024)

Known Public Footprint

GitHub: echocanhelp

Maintains wiki-public repository (Echopedia)


Facebook: juniorhsu

Areas of Work

Community historical documentation and oral history
Digital infrastructure for public memory (Echopedia / Quartz wiki)
Identity verification and contributor workflows (LINE-first)
Lightweight, low-maintenance systems for volunteer organizations

Echopedia Role
Primary architect and maintainer of Echopedia, the community knowledge base for TAHS and related Taiwanese American organizations. Responsible for page creation standards, Chinese + romanized name formatting, and publishing workflows.
Revision History

2026-05-26: Initial draft scaffold
2026-05-28: Updated with confirmed TAHS President role, family details, and location history. Status changed to Published.
2026-06-16: Corrected prior attribution error; restored Leonard Hsu Jr.’s Chinese name to 許景鴻 (Hsu Ching-Hung) and removed Rex Chen’s Chinese name from this page.
